> **What you can defend when you leave.** Adapt one defensible claim to one audience and rehearse defending it against real questions.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

A claim becomes public the moment an audience can question it, and audiences do not read contracts. They read posters, hear talks, scan briefs, and ask hard questions. This milestone adapts your bounded claims to the format your venue asks for and rehearses the defense before it counts. The poster lessons carry the fully worked example; the milestone's venue contract and content map carry every other format. The rehearsal record matters as much as the artifact: the questions you cannot answer yet are the truest map of what remains.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 10: Your defense, ready](milestone10-adapt-and-defend.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** A short venue contract, one chosen-format adaptation that satisfies it - poster, talk, brief, or another - a content map tracing every load-bearing claim and number, and a defense rehearsal record. This is not yet public release.

Milestone 11 lets strangers rerun what you have just defended, which is the one test rehearsal cannot give you. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## Choosing your format

Start with a **venue contract**: your written record of what the
audience will receive and what the venue allows. Name the audience,
the medium, the length or space limit, the required elements, the
accessibility needs, the submission rule, and the question channel.
One line each is enough. Example: a five-minute recorded talk, six
slides, captions required, no live questions.

Every format carries the same research core: the bounded claim, the
evidence that earns it, uncertainty and limitations, traceable
numbers and citations, and whatever disclosure or permission
information the audience needs. The format only decides where those
pieces live. Choose the row that fits your venue, work the lessons it
names, and when you borrow a technique from another row, name the
technique rather than claiming the whole lesson transfers.

| If your venue asks for | build it with | then test and rehearse |
|---|---|---|
| a poster | Research Posters | Poster Criticism, then Difficult Questions |
| a live talk or pitch | Research Pitches | Difficult Questions, spoken |
| a talk with slides | Research Pitches; every quantitative visual follows the poster lesson's figure rules | Difficult Questions, spoken |
| a written brief or one-pager | your Studio 9 note compressed to the contract, with the poster lesson's figure rules for any figure | Difficult Questions, in writing |
| another format | the venue contract plus the nearest row, naming what transfers | Difficult Questions, in the venue's own mode |

The poster lessons are this book's fully worked example: one surface,
no narrator, every number exposed. Difficult Questions is for
everyone. If your venue has no live questions, the rehearsal still
happens: have a peer or an AI reviewer send you hard questions in
writing, and record defend, concede, or do-not-know for each.


## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 10; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 31 — Research Posters](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/27-research-posters.html): if your venue is a poster, or your format carries a quantitative figure: the draft with labeled values, uncertainty shown as the design licenses (interval or caveat), and a headline verbed to your boundary.
- [Lesson 32 — Poster Criticism](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/28-poster-criticism.html): if your venue is a poster: the gallery-walk audit of your draft, hits ranked by how far the error travels, fixed once, and the lock call.
- [Lesson 33 — Research Pitches](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/29-research-pitches.html): if you will speak: your 30-second and 3-minute pitches, built boundary-first and tested aloud on an outsider.
- [Lesson 34 — Difficult Questions and Uncertainty](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part5-communicating/30-difficult-questions-and-uncertainty.html): your five hardest fair questions with defend-or-concede answers, and your uncertainty-and-limitations statement in ULN form.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
